source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Normal variation in patient assignment alone, without unusual controlled-substance access, waste, or count patterns.","B":"Repeated controlled-substance count discrepancies or unusual wasting patterns that warrant investigation for diversion.","C":"Consistently reconciled controlled-substance records with expected use patterns and no unexplained inventory differences.","D":"Working on a unit where controlled substances are rarely used, without unusual access, documentation, or inventory events."}}
source_row.rationale: Repeated unexplained controlled-substance discrepancies, atypical access/administration or unusual waste patterns are recognized diversion red flags that warrant investigation; no single pattern alone proves diversion.
source_row.source_detail: DEA diversion case describes manipulation of controlled-substance dispensing/waste processes and discrepancies; such unexplained transactional patterns warrant institutional investigation rather than assumptions from paperwork alone. Official DEA diversion-control enforcement material; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: U.S. DEA — Health-Care Diversion Enforcement Example
source_row.stem: Which pattern should prompt investigation for possible controlled-substance diversion rather than being dismissed because documentation appears complete?
